verdict: Carrier sales rose 12% to $6.3B on booming data-center demand, but a $3.1B goodwill write-down in Europe swung it to a $2.6B GAAP loss — underlying adjusted EPS was $0.87.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue $6,263M vs $5,579M a year ago; organic sales +15%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted continuing operations, vs $0.47 a year ago

kpis.label: Backlog
kpis.note: a record, up about 60% YoY; total orders up about 35%

segments.name: Climate Solutions Americas
segments.note: Heating, cooling and refrigeration in the Americas — sales up 24% (25% organic) on residential and commercial strength and about $120M of tariff (IEEPA) refund benefits; segment profit up 40% to $745M.

segments.name: Climate Solutions Europe
segments.note: Europe climate sales up 3% — 12% organic growth partly offset by divestitures and currency. Segment profit rose 40% to $168M, but this is the unit that took the goodwill write-down below.

segments.name: Climate Solutions Asia Pacific, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Sales up 2% (3% organic) — commercial up 10%, partly offset by weaker residential and light commercial. Segment profit $103M.

segments.name: Climate Solutions Transportation
segments.note: Refrigeration for trucks, trailers and containers — sales down 3% as container growth was outweighed by truck and trailer weakness. Segment profit $117M.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company — down from $803M a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new climate and refrigeration products — about flat.

opex.name: Goodwill impairment & other, net
opex.note: A $3,100M non-cash goodwill impairment on Climate Solutions Europe, less $57M of equity-method earnings, plus $1M of other expense — all of which sit inside GAAP operating profit.

takeaways.title: Orders and backlog hit records
takeaways.text: Total orders rose about 35% and data-center orders about 300%, taking backlog above $8.5B, up about 60% YoY. Carrier also signed long-term agreements worth multiple billions with minimum volume commitments, on top of backlog.

takeaways.title: A Europe write-down drove the GAAP loss
takeaways.text: A non-cash $3.1B goodwill impairment on Climate Solutions Europe turned a profitable operating quarter into a $2,273M GAAP operating loss. Excluding it and other items, adjusted operating profit was $1,091M, up 33%, at a 17.4% margin.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS grew 30%
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $0.87 vs $0.67 a year ago, helped by about $130M of tariff (IEEPA) refunds in operating profit. Free cash flow was $674M and Carrier returned about $600M to shareholders.

oneTimers: Goodwill impairment of $3,100M (non-cash) on the Climate Solutions Europe reporting unit — the entire reason for the GAAP loss; it is excluded from adjusted results.

About $130M of operating-profit benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds in the quarter (about $120M of it in Climate Solutions Americas); adjusted EPS includes about a $0.10 benefit from the refunds, net of a $0.02 noncontrolling-interest effect.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $93M, partly offset by a $3M non-service pension benefit — a net $90M cost. The flow uses the total net loss of $2,540M (all from continuing operations); after $53M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests, the loss attributable to Carrier shareholders was $2,593M (-$3.16 per share).
footerNote: Tax was still a $177M expense despite the pre-tax loss, because the goodwill impairment is largely non-deductible.
